A.explanation: The combined regime pairs a hostile parent framework — binary-sex passport policy upheld Nov 2025, an entry cable authorising refusal on sex doubt and lifetime fraud findings, federally funded single-sex facility exclusion, corrections conversion-therapy policy and documented immigration-custody abuse — with a territory that adds no hostile layer. Locally there is no sodomy offence, no facility ban, an institutionalised fa'afafine tradition, Pride since 2016, and federal employment remedies that actually reached the territorial government. Social friction is conservative religiosity, not threat-framing. Parent universal exposures (entry screening, federal facilities) persist at every crossing, holding the score below acceptance-with-protections tiers.

entry_documents.exposure: Parent cable (24 Feb 2025): document discrepancy or reasonable doubt on sex → refuse case, request evidence; possible lifetime fraud ineligibility. X markers unprocessed; airport screening routinely outs trans travellers. Applies at territorial entry.
entry_documents.protection: No territorial document hostility; records office changes birth-certificate markers on medical documentation. Foreign X passports remain valid to expiry.
entry_documents.interaction: Territory sits under federal border control, so parent refusal rules govern entry; a mismatch here becomes a federal fraud question, not a local one.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections bureau's conversion-therapy-style policy (hair, hormones, psychiatric substitution) and documented immigration-custody forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse apply to anyone entering federal custody, including here.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: No territorial custody hostility documented; federal employment-discrimination settlement (Sep 2023) shows federal enforcement reaching this government.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: A visitor detained for any reason enters federal custody regimes; territorial institutions do not shield them.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Parent executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities; reaches federally funded sites on the islands. No territorial ban documented, but conservative religious norms may produce informal friction.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Territory has no facility ban; fa'afafine recognised as integral to culture; Pride and pageants draw family support.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal facility rule governs federally funded venues regardless of local acceptance, so local tolerance cannot cancel it.

care_services.exposure: Parent measures (minors' care framed as mutilation, funding freezes, hospital-record subpoenas) apply federally; territory-specific care access for visitors is not sourced.
care_services.protection: No territorial denial of care documented.
care_services.interaction: Any federally funded clinic or insurance pathway here inherits the parent restrictions.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Parent counterterrorism language on 'radically pro-transgender' groups and official hostility create a national threat-framing climate advocates compare to early genocide stages.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: No local official hostility documented; cultural inclusion of fa'afafine, elected acceptance, federal law-enforcement intervention on the island.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Federal framing can reach local police training and cooperation even where local opinion is tolerant.

minors_guardians.exposure: Parent order directs criminal investigation/prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition, plus care bans in 27 state/provinces; a parent travelling with a trans minor carries these federal exposures directly.
minors_guardians.protection: No territorial measure against trans minors documented; age of consent 16 regardless of orientation.
minors_guardians.interaction: Territorial schools are not the target, but federal charging authority extends into the territory.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: One Feb 2023 sexual-abuse charge against a 16-year-old trans teenager, no outcome stated; conservative religious society; only 23 state/provinces carry state-level GI bias statutes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal gender-identity hate-crime statute and employment protections operate; no pattern of violence against trans people documented locally; small, familiar community.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Federal hate-crime recourse exists but coverage depends on federal willingness to act.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Parent passport, EO and health-rule challenges unresolved; practical exposure varies with what is in force on travel dates; no local prevalence data on discrimination or attitudes.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ on document rules; functioning federal courts; two documented federal remedies against the territorial government; ACLU suit pending.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Local remedies worked in employment; unknown whether they extend to visitor-facing document or facility issues.

anchor_checks.comparison: No public-decency statute criminalising presentation, no routine arrest on document mismatch, no months-long pretrial custody or coerced confessions here. Custody abuse exists only in federal immigration/corrections contexts, not as the ordinary path after routine discovery, so far above this anchor.

No visitor entry register or blanket admission bar; entry exposure is discretionary refusal on document doubt, not a categorical trans exclusion, and no appeal-to-same-agency dead end. Local acceptance and no facility ban push above this exclusion-tier anchor.

Parent entry screening (secondary inspection, possible refusal, fraud referral) plus federally funded facility exclusion matches this anchor's humiliating administrative exposure — but the territory adds documented cultural acceptance and working federal remedies the anchor lacks, so modestly above.

Would need operative visitor-facing document acceptance and trained, appealable inspection. Here the parent passport regime and entry cable remain in force, corrections and immigration custody harm is documented, and federal facility exclusion applies, so materially below.

A.synthesis: The territory contributes no hostile layer of its own: no sodomy offence, no facility ban, an embedded third-gender tradition, and federal remedies that demonstrably reached the territorial government. That moves it above the parent's baseline. But the combined regime is still governed by parent instruments the visitor cannot avoid — entry screening keyed to sex doubt, the binary passport policy upheld by the Supreme Court, federally funded single-sex facility exclusion, and federal custody conditions including conversion-therapy-style policies and documented immigration abuse. Local tolerance mitigates street exposure and social friction; it cannot mitigate border, federal-facility or custody exposure. The result is reduced but not low risk: everyday local life is broadly safe, institutional encounters at entry and in federal settings are not.

B.explanation: The national seat applies the parent regime directly: binary-sex passport policy in force, an entry cable authorising refusal on sex doubt and lifetime fraud findings, federally funded single-sex facility exclusion, corrections conversion-therapy policy and documented immigration-custody abuse. The division adds its own hostile layer — a facilities restriction attached by the national legislature that the local council cannot repeal, with trans-rights protesters arrested at the legislature building on 5 December 2024. Local mitigation is thin: a caveated July 2026 low-risk ranking, no local sodomy offence, no local document hostility. Local hate-crime, police-practice and custody conditions are undocumented, not safe.

entry_documents.exposure: Parent Feb 2025 passport binary policy and 24 Feb 2025 cable: sex doubt → refuse case; possible lifetime fraud finding; X markers unprocessed; airport screening outs trans travellers. National law applies directly inside the seat.
entry_documents.protection: No division-level document hostility documented; July 2026 assessment lists it among units not targeting trans adults.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry is federal in both dossiers; the division's local council cannot soften border practice.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Federal corrections conversion-therapy-style policy and documented immigration-custody forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and sexual abuse apply. Locally, trans-rights activists were arrested at the legislature building on 5 Dec 2024.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Local custody conditions and police practice are not sourced; no local custody abuse documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Anyone detained here falls under federal custody regimes; local ranking does not reach federal facilities.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: A facilities restriction is in force in this division, attached by the national legislature rather than the local council and therefore locally unrepealable; scope, enforcement and visitor reach are unsourced. Parent EO separately bars federally funded single-sex facilities.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The division has no bathroom ban of its own; the July 2026 assessment ranks it low-risk, caveated by override risk.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Two overlapping sovereigns impose facility exclusion here — national legislature attachment plus parent executive order — with no local repeal path.

care_services.exposure: Parent measures (minors' care executive order, funding freezes, proposed insurance bar, hospital-record subpoenas) apply directly within the division; local care access for visitors is not sourced.
care_services.interaction: National executive orders operate inside the seat with no local buffer.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Parent counterterrorism language on 'radically pro-transgender' groups and broader hostile posture apply directly; enforcement already reached protest activity at the legislature building in Dec 2024.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: July 2026 assessment lists the division among units largely refraining from targeting trans adults, with an explicit durability caveat.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: National legislature and executive act directly on this jurisdiction, so favourable local standing can be overtaken without local law changing.

minors_guardians.exposure: Parent order directing criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition, care bans in 27 state/provinces and proposed insurance bar apply directly inside the division; a travelling family carries these federal exposures.
minors_guardians.protection: No division-level measure against trans minors documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: National charging and funding authority operates within the seat; local council cannot displace it.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented locally; parent records show only partial state-level bias-statute coverage and Dec 2024 protest arrests. Absence of local incidents is silence, not evidence of safety in a small, highly visible jurisdiction.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Federal gender-identity hate-crime statute and 2020 employment ruling operate nationally.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Federal protections reach the division, but enforcement practice by local police is unsourced.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Facilities-restriction scope and enforcement unsourced; local protections overrideable by national legislature and executive orders; low-risk ranking method unverifiable; parent challenges unresolved.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Functioning federal courts, pending ACLU suit, legal-aid FAQ on document rules, and a caveated low-risk placement.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies a visitor would need are federal and slow, while the exposures are immediate and locally unrepealable.

anchor_checks.comparison: No presentation-decency statute, no routine arrest on mismatch, no months-long pretrial custody or coerced confessions documented. Custody abuse exists only in federal custody contexts. Far above this anchor.

Entry exposure resembles this anchor's discretionary administrative exclusion — refusal on sex doubt with appeal to the same authority — and the division adds a locally unrepealable facility restriction plus protest arrests. Similar in kind to the register anchor, though no categorical trans-entry ban, so about level.

Parent secondary screening and possible entry refusal match this anchor's humiliating administrative tier, but the division's own facility attachment, protest arrests, undocumented police practice and no local acceptance tradition sit it below this anchor's mixed-but-functioning picture.

Would need trained inspection, appealable detention and compensation. Here the parent document regime, facility exclusion from two sovereigns, custody-harm record and unverifiable local protections place it well below.

B.synthesis: The seat inherits the parent's universal exposures with no local buffer: binary passport policy, entry refusal on sex doubt with possible fraud referral, federally funded facility exclusion, hostile federal framing and federal custody conditions including documented abuse. It then adds a division-specific hostile layer — a facilities restriction attached by the national legislature that the local council cannot repeal, enforced at least once through the December 2024 protest arrests. Its only documented mitigation is a caveated July 2026 low-risk ranking and the absence of local sodomy or document offences; local police, custody and violence records are simply missing, and silence is not safety. Compared with A, this dossier lacks the cultural acceptance tradition, has no demonstrated local remedy reaching visitors, and carries an extra enforced exclusion layer, so it rates materially lower.
